card.statement:
Given ${\mathcal{C}}$ and ${\mathcal{D}}$ two finite semisimple linear 2-categories, there exists a finite semisimple linear 2-category ${\mathcal{C}}\boxdot{\mathcal{D}}$ and linear 2-functor $\boxdot\colon{\mathcal{C}}\times{\mathcal{D}}\to{\mathcal{C}}\boxdot{\mathcal{D}}$ such that precomposition with $\boxdot$ induces an equivalence

$\Hom({\mathcal{C}}\boxdot{\mathcal{D}},{\mathcal{E}})\simeq\Hom_{\textit{bilin}}({\mathcal{C}}\times{\mathcal{D}},{\mathcal{E}})$

for all finite ${\mathcal{E}}$. This equivalence is natural in all three variables. Unpacked, this means:

•

For every finite 2-category ${\mathcal{E}}$ and bilinear bi-2-functor ${\mathcal{F}}\colon{\mathcal{C}}\times{\mathcal{D}}$ there exists a 2-functor $\bar{\mathcal{F}}\colon{\mathcal{C}}\boxdot{\mathcal{D}}\to{\mathcal{E}}$ and 2-natural equivalence $u\colon\bar{F}\circ\boxdot\Rightarrow F$.

•

For every two functors ${\mathcal{G}},{\mathcal{H}}\colon{\mathcal{C}}\boxdot{\mathcal{D}}\to{\mathcal{E}}$ and 2-natural transformation $\tau\colon{\mathcal{G}}\circ\boxdot\Rightarrow{\mathcal{H}}\circ\boxdot$, there exists a 2-natural equivalence $\tau^{\prime}\colon{\mathcal{G}}\to{\mathcal{H}}$ and invertible modification $\Sigma\colon\tau^{\prime}\circ\boxdot\Rrightarrow\tau$.

•

Finally, for every two 2-natural transformations $\tau,\tau^{\prime}\colon{\mathcal{G}}\to{\mathcal{H}}$ and modification $\Pi\colon\tau\circ\boxdot\rightarrow\tau^{\prime}\circ\boxdot$, there exists a unique invertible modification $\Pi^{\prime}\colon\tau\to\tau$ such that $\Pi^{\prime}\circ\boxdot=\Pi$.

Furthermore:

•

If ${\mathcal{C}}$ and ${\mathcal{D}}$ are monoidal, then so is ${\mathcal{C}}\boxdot{\mathcal{D}}$. With this monoidal structure, the 2-functor $\boxdot$ is monoidal.

•

If ${\mathcal{F}}\colon{\mathcal{C}}\times{\mathcal{D}}\to{\mathcal{E}}$ is monoidal, then so is the induced 2-functor $\bar{F}\colon{\mathcal{C}}\boxdot{\mathcal{D}}\to{\mathcal{E}}$

Finally, for finite semisimple linear monoidal 1-categories $A,B$, then

${\sf Mod}(A)\boxdot{\sf Mod}(B)\simeq{\sf Mod}(A\boxtimes B)$

and this equivalence is natural in $A$ in $B$.

We provide details of these constructions in Appendix A.

Construction 3.7.

The Deligne 2-tensor product, together with the symmetric monoidal structure on ${\sf 2Vec}$ give ${\sf 2Slice}$ the structure of a symmetric monoidal 2-category.
card.label: Theorem 3.6

paper.title: Tannaka-Krein reconstruction for fusion 2-categories
paper.abstract: We reprove the classical Tannaka-Krein reconstruction theorem by finding a monoidal equivalence of categories between a 1-truncated sub-2-category of the slice 2-category ${\sf Mod}({\sf Vec})/{\sf Vec}$ and the category of algebras. We then immediately generalize this approach to find a monoidal equivalence of 2-categories between a 2-truncated sub-3-category of the slice 3-category ${\sf Mod}({\sf TwoVec})/{\sf TwoVec}$ and the category of algebras. As an immediate consequence, a finite semisimple 2-Hopf algebra $C$ can be recovered from its fusion 2-category of modules together with the monoidal fiber 2-functor to ${\sf TwoVec}$. Moreover, every fusion 2-category equipped with a monoidal functor to ${\sf TwoVec}$ is of this form.
